key_insight: For shape-informed hemodynamic surrogates, active learning and finite-element physical consistency are more effective during fine-tuning than during early or full-training use.
engineering_relevance: The workflow supports scalable, patient-specific prediction of aortic velocity and pressure fields at peak systole across varying vascular anatomies.
method: Generate physiologically consistent CFD data from SynthAorta geometries using automatic boundary-condition adjustment.
Represent anatomies as displacement fields from a common reference and train Graph U-Net and Transformer U-Net surrogates.
Explore gradient- and subspace-based active learning alongside differentiable finite-element residual constraints.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved fine-tuning performance from active learning and physical consistency constraints, while out-of-distribution tests identify geometric parametrization support as the main limitation; no quantitative metrics are provided.
watch_item: Generalization to unfamiliar anatomies depends on the geometric coverage of the underlying parametrization, not just the network architecture.
paper_title: Synthetic Dataset Generation, Physical Consistency and Active Learning for Shape-Informed Surrogate Modeling of Hemodynamics
